value: Civil Code (BGB), tenancy chapter, §§ 535 ff. Residential rent rules including deposit, rent increases and termination are in the BGB.
Security may not exceed three times the monthly rent, excluding service charges paid as a flat rate or advance (§ 551(1) BGB).

Landlord must invest a cash deposit with a bank at the rate usual for savings deposits with three months notice, separate from the landlord's own assets; the tenant may pay in three equal monthly instalments (§ 551(2)-(3) BGB).

Landlord may ask for consent to a rise up to the local comparative rent if the rent has been unchanged for 15 months; the request may be made at the earliest one year after the last increase (§ 558(1) BGB).

Rent may not rise by more than 20 percent within three years (15 percent in areas designated by Land governments as having endangered housing supply), excluding modernisation and service-charge changes (§ 558(3) BGB).

field: Rent at start of tenancy in tight markets
value: In areas with a tight housing market designated by a Land ordinance, rent at the start of a tenancy may exceed the local comparative rent by at most 10 percent (§ 556d(1) BGB). Designations are made by each Land, so they differ by municipality.

Landlord may terminate only with a legitimate interest (e.g. tenant breach, own use) and not to raise rent (§ 573 BGB). Notice is three months, extended by three months after five and again after eight years of tenancy (§ 573c BGB).

An energy certificate must be issued when a building or dwelling is let, unless a valid one already exists (§ 80(3) of the Building Energy Act; the official page shows the act under the title Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz - GModG).

value: Law 29/1994 of 24 November on Urban Leases (LAU).

Term is freely agreed, but if shorter than five years (seven if the landlord is a legal entity) the lease is extended by yearly periods until it reaches five (seven) years, unless the tenant gives 30 days notice (art. 9 LAU).
A cash deposit equal to one month of rent is mandatory for housing (two months for non-residential lets) (art. 36(1) LAU).

For housing leases up to five years (seven for legal-entity landlords) any additional guarantee may not exceed two months of rent; one month for temporary lets; the tenant cannot be required to take rent-default insurance (art. 36(5) LAU).
Rent may be updated only on each anniversary and as agreed; without express agreement no update applies. The increase may not exceed the annual change in the IRAV reference index (art. 18 LAU).

At the end of the mandatory or tacit extension, a tenant in documented social and economic vulnerability may request a one-year extraordinary extension, which large holders must accept (art. 10(2) LAU). In declared stressed residential market zones, the tenant may request an extraordinary extension during the period the zone declaration is in force (art. 10(3) LAU). Zones are declared under Law 12/2023 by the competent authorities.

value: Law 431/1998 (residential leases) and Law 392/1978 (lease provisions, including the deposit).
The security deposit may not exceed three months of rent, and it bears legal interest payable to the tenant at the end of each year (art. 11, Law 392/1978).

Parties may sign leases of at least four years, renewed for a further four years unless the landlord uses a ground in art. 3 (own use, sale and similar) (art. 2(1), Law 431/1998). At the second expiry either party may seek renewal on new terms or decline renewal by registered letter at least six months before expiry.

As an alternative, parties may agree rent, duration and conditions under local agreements between landlord and tenant organisations (art. 2(3), Law 431/1998); for these contracts any rent above the maximum set by the local agreements is void (art. 13(4)).

At the first expiry the landlord may refuse renewal on listed grounds (e.g. use by the landlord or close relatives, sale on the art. 3 terms, building works) with at least six months notice (art. 3(1), Law 431/1998).

Any agreement setting rent above the amount in the written and registered contract is void, and the tenant may reclaim the excess within six months of returning the property (art. 13(1)-(2), Law 431/1998).

field: Rent above 3 percent of replacement value
value: An increase taking annual rent above 3 percent of the dwelling's replacement value is allowed only in justified cases listed in art. 8a(4a) and (4e); on written request the landlord must state the reason and calculation within 14 days (art. 8a(4)).
